owner_posts.post_text: In a world that’s always ‘on,’ the real strength today is knowing when to pause. Feeling mentally drained doesn’t mean you’re failing — it means you’ve been carrying too much for too long. Give yourself permission to rest, unplug, and breathe. Protecting your peace is productivity too.

Summer can affect mental health in different ways. For some people, sunshine and longer days may improve mood. For others, rising temperatures can worsen anxiety, low mood, irritability, fatigue, and poor sleep.

Heat places extra stress on the body, can disturb sleep, and may intensify physical sensations like a racing heart or restlessness, which can feel similar to anxiety. Poor sleep during warmer nights can also affect concentration, emotional balance, and energy levels.

At the same time, simple protective habits can make a real difference: staying hydrated, keeping a regular routine, gentle movement, rest, and spending time in calming natural spaces.

In simple terms: summer can boost mood when the body is well-regulated. Prioritising sleep, hydration, and rest is not just self-care~it is mental health care.

We at Mindsight encourage you to stay hydrated, slow down when needed, and take gentle care of your mind and body this summer. ☀️

Sitting with your feelings means noticing them, allowing them, and understanding they will pass.

Name the emotion, feel it without judgment, and meet yourself with kindness. 💙

In this community, every feeling is valid and welcome.

Resilience check-in 🌱

We often think resilient people have it all together… but the truth is, they feel overwhelmed too.

Resilience isn’t about avoiding hard moments – it’s about how we move through them, in our own time and in our own way.

Feel free to share, reflect, or just pause here for a moment. You don’t have to have it all figured out. 🌱

In a world that’s always ‘on,’ the real strength today is knowing when to pause. Feeling mentally drained doesn’t mean you’re failing — it means you’ve been carrying too much for too long. Give yourself permission to rest, unplug, and breathe. Protecting your peace is productivity too.

Setting boundaries isn’t selfish — it’s essential. When you protect your time, energy, and emotional space, you protect your mental health. Saying no, stepping back, or choosing yourself is not wrong; it’s healthy. Boundaries help you breathe, heal, and grow.

Therapists want you to know this:

•Choosing therapy isn’t weakness — it’s quiet courage.
•It’s the strength of saying, I deserve to feel lighter.
•Healing begins the moment you decide you don’t have to carry it alone.

Self-Discipline vs Self-Compassion: 

Which one actually helps you stay consistent?

We’re often taught that strict self-discipline and self-criticism are the keys to success. 

But research and clinical experience show that self-compassion—being kind, understanding, and realistic with yourself—actually leads to better consistency over time. 

When you respond to mistakes with curiosity instead of harsh judgment, you reduce shame, build emotional safety, and make it easier to try again.

Self-discipline rooted in self-compassion isn’t about “letting yourself off the hook”; it’s about supporting yourself in a way that makes growth sustainable, not exhausting. 🌱
When your mind feels full and you don’t know where to start… therapy helps you sort the mess, piece by piece. You don’t have to hold everything together all the time. 💐

The first and most important step in resolving any issue is identifying the problem. Minal Mishra madam approached our situation methodically, speaking to all the concerned parties with empathy and insight. She demonstrated a deep understanding of the dynamics at play in NRI families, including the cultural contrasts between Western and Indian values. From the beginning, we felt she was the right person for this delicate task.

What truly sets Minal madam apart is her unbiased approach, remarkable patience, and sincere commitment to helping families heal. She creates a safe, respectful space for everyone to express themselves. Unless one party is completely unwilling to engage in the process or the issue is extraordinarily severe, I can confidently say that she has the ability to bring people together and help them find a harmonious path forward.

Minal madam is a gem in Dr. Kiran’s Mind Centre. We are deeply grateful for her support and guidance. Thanks to her, we now look forward to a more peaceful and loving future with our family.

featured_reviews.name: Alka Shettigar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I chose this clinic based on its positive online reviews, which is why it seems Important to share my experience for anyone considering counselling here.

I approached the clinic as I was experiencing a temporary dip in motivation . My therapist was Mansi . After a single exploratory session, I was advised to take the MCMI assessment.

Unfortunately, my experience was disappointing from both a professional and clinical perspective.

To begin with, I had to follow up consistently to obtain the results. There was no proactive communication from the clinic. My name and contact details had been incorrectly recorded which immediately raised concerns about professionalism.

What concerned me was the way the assessment results were handled. During a brief Call , I was given Some  serious labels. When I asked for  examples from our Only counselling discussion that supported these conclusions, I did not receive any clear or logical explanation.

What I found most disappointing was the lack of empathy and nuance in communication. Counselling requires sensitivity, context, and careful interpretation of tests . Instead, the experience felt rushed, overly reductionist, and lacking the depth I would expect from a professional mental health service.

I have previously worked with therapists and understand the difference between being challenged and being understood. In this case, I left feeling neither understood nor supported.

Others May have had “positive experiences “here, but my experience was very very different. Kindly  verify carefully before proceeding .
